content:
The image shows a soybean seedling at soil level. Key observations:

- Very young seedling emerging from wet/saturated soil
- The hypocotyl (stem just above soil) appears water-soaked, pinched, and collapsed
- The seedling is wilted and unable to stand — classic "damping-off" posture
- Roots appear brown and rotted
- Soil looks very wet and compacted, consistent with conditions favoring water mold pathogens
- No leaf lesions visible — the damage is at the stem/root interface at or below soil line

This matches **Pythium damping-off** very well: pre- or post-emergence damping-off caused by Pythium spp. presents as water-soaked, pinched hypocotyls in wet soils, causing seedling collapse before or just after emergence. Rhizoctonia also causes damping-off but typically shows a dry, reddish-brown sunken lesion ("wire stem") rather than the water-soaked collapse seen here. The saturated soil and water-soaked appearance strongly favor Pythium.
